# Preface {.unnumbered}

Machine learning systems usually end at digital output. A classifier emits a probability distribution. A language model emits text. A vision model emits a bounding box. The digital software surrounding them may be complex, but the inference itself does not move the world.

**Physical AI Systems** begin when that digital endpoint moves. The learned model's output becomes a proposal for physical action. If permitted, that action consumes electrical and mechanical energy, moves physical matter, interacts with humans, and permanently mutates the physical world ($W_t \to W_{t+1}$).

The moment an action changes the world, it alters all future observations endogenously ($A_t \to W_{t+1} \to O_{t+1}$). The system must now live with the irreversible consequences of its own decisions. **You cannot `ctrl+z` kinetic energy.**

---

## The Durable Question

This book is not about training bigger models in simulation, nor is it a survey of robot kinematics. The durable question governing every chapter, interface, and laboratory in this text is:

> **"What must the surrounding system know, measure, enforce, preserve, and prove before an unverified learned proposal may produce a physical consequence?"**

---

## The 4 Bedrock Laws of Physical AI Systems

Every architectural pattern, mathematical contract, and firmware check in this book is anchored in four physical laws:

::: {.callout-objective}
**Law 1: The Law of Physical Causality and Irreversibility.** Software state can be caught with a `try/catch` block or rewound. Physical actions ($W_t \to W_{t+1}$) governed by mass, inertia, friction ($\mu$), and gravity ($g$) are permanent and irreversible. Every action mutates the environment, consumes energy, and shifts the distribution of future sensory observations.
:::

::: {.callout-decision}
**Law 2: The Law of Information Freshness (The Time Law).** The physical world does not pause while an AI model computes. Sensor observations age the microsecond they are sampled. Mean latency is a dangerous lie; tail latency ($P_{99}$), memory bus contention, and information age ($\Delta t$) dictate physical closed-loop stability and dynamic stopping distances ($d_{\text{stop}}$).
:::

::: {.callout-contract}
**Law 3: The Law of Proposal–Permission Privilege (The Architecture Law).** No stochastic, learned neural network (VLM, VLA, or Diffusion Policy) may hold direct physical authority over actuators. Learned models running on application processors (MPU) are *untrusted proposal services*. Real-time physical permission belongs exclusively to dedicated, zero-allocation microcontrollers (MCU) running deterministic safety envelopes and physical fallbacks.
:::

::: {.callout-autopsy}
**Law 4: The Law of Governed Change and Defensible Release (The Safety Law).** A physical agent shapes its own future data. Naive training on raw logs without isolating safety interventions induces severe covariate shift and policy collapse. A cherry-picked video demo or simulation benchmark is not evidence of safety; release requires cross-layer fault injection and a Claim-Argument-Evidence (CAE) safety case rendering an accountable **Deploy / Condition / Refuse** verdict.
:::

## What This Book Is (and Is Not)

To keep our systems focus razor-sharp, we maintain strict boundaries:

| What This Book Is NOT | What This Book IS |
| :--- | :--- |
| **Not** a 50-page derivation of robot arm kinematics or Denavit-Hartenberg matrices. | A systems manual on **multi-rate runtimes, latency tails, and proposal-permission boundaries**. |
| **Not** a guide to training 70B foundation models from scratch on GPU clusters. | An architectural blueprint for **integrating modern VLMs/VLAs as untrusted components**. |
| **Not** a software tutorial on cloud LLM prompt chaining or chatbot wrappers. | A hands-on guide to **zero-copy DMA, shared memory IPC, FreeRTOS safety filters, and watchdogs**. |
| **Not** pure physics simulation in Python (Isaac Gym, PyBullet). | A physical engineering discipline validated on **bench hardware with real mass, friction, and lag**. |
| **Not** a decorative compliance checklist. | A rigorous methodology for building a **Cumulative Design Dossier** and defending a release verdict. |

---

## Concept vs. Realization: The Anatomy of a Physical Agent & The Physical AI Kit

This work is organized around two complementary pillars:

| The Conceptual Framework<br>*(The Anatomy of a Physical Agent)* | The Reference Hardware Realization<br>*(The Physical Agent on the Physical AI Kit)* |
| :--- | :--- |
| **1. The Causal Boundary & Loop** | Actuator power bus isolation and hardware emergency stop loop (`LOOP-01`) |
| **2. Sensory-Motor Metrology** | Hardware ingestion, PTP timestamps, and complete-path $P_{99}$ latency profiler (`REQ-01`) |
| **3. Multi-Rate Runtime Engine** | Dual-Brain lock-free IPC skeleton (Linux MPU $\leftrightarrow$ FreeRTOS MCU) (`RUN-01`) |
| **4. Spatial Affordance Tokens** | Edge NPU spatial vision and contact encoder tokenizers (`OBS-01`) |
| **5. Temporal Belief & World Memory** | 3D dynamic coordinate frame graph ($SE(3)$) and state validity TTL leases (`STATE-01`) |
| **6. Deliberation & Semantic Intent (S2)** | MPU VLM spatial bounding boxes and expiring intent leases ($t_{\text{expire}}$) (`INTENT-01`) |
| **7. Motor Planning (S1.5)** | MPU VLA multi-step action chunk unrolling ($H$-steps) and $\mathcal{C}^2$ ensembling (`PLAN-01`) |
| **8. Real-Time Reflex (S1)** | Dedicated MCU bare-metal 1 kHz safety enforcer and dynamic stopping bounds ($d_{\text{stop}}$) (`ENF-01`) |
| **9. Silicon Placement Map** | Whole-system heterogeneous resource ledger (FLOPs, SRAM, Watts, bus QoS) (`PLACE-01`) |
| **10. Human Authority & Lineage** | Bumpless joystick override state machine and cryptographic provenance logger (`AUTH-01`) |
| **11. Defensible Release Gate** | Cross-layer injected seeded fault defense and CAE safety case (`REL-01`) |
